issues.finding: Rolling-return treatment and the latest-values summary row were underdefined.
issues.rationale: The market criterion now permits explained N/A values when the t-12 observation is outside the retrieved source window and separately requires a latest-values summary row with date differences disclosed.

issues.finding: The memo could omit specifically required market measures.
issues.rationale: The memo rubric now enumerates all instructed yield, slope, timing, policy-rate, real-rate, return, and period-high evidence without prescribing conclusions.

issues.finding: Exact workbook and memo filenames were not enforced.
issues.rationale: The final memo row now requires all three exact filenames and formats, and the page-limit criterion names client_memo.pdf directly.

issues.finding: The Unit Matching Matrix candidate population was not auditable.
issues.rationale: The criterion now requires either the full unit roster or a reproducible candidate-selection rule covering assigned, closest eligible, unavailable, and specialty-relevant units.

issues.finding: Benchmark flags were not explicitly required per supplier-item quote.
issues.rationale: The line-item criterion now requires a separate four-label classification for every supplier-item quote.

issues.finding: The exact three-sheet workbook structure was not enforced.
issues.rationale: The split-analysis row now begins with an exact sheet-set requirement for the bid evaluation workbook.

issues.finding: The briefing table could omit equally productive and less productive discrepancies.
issues.rationale: The criterion now requires separate rows for all three published productivity categories with values, variances, and plausible explanations.

issues.finding: The lowest-performing program lacked a program-level quarterly aggregation rule.
issues.rationale: The criterion now requires a documented full-year program-level aggregation, accepts defensible alternatives, and rejects an unexplained single minimum row.

issues.finding: Declining Level 3 outcomes lacked a consistent trend definition.
issues.rationale: The schedule criterion now requires a stated program-level full-year decline rule, accepts equivalent documented methods, and prevents an unexplained single adjacent-quarter dip from controlling.

issues.finding: Quarterly demand could be compared directly with weekly capacity.
issues.rationale: The risk criterion now requires peak weekly demand or an explicitly time-normalized equivalent and separately requires identification of the lowest-capacity instructor.

issues.finding: Visible use of the attendance template was subjective.
issues.rationale: The criterion now checks concrete training-information and attendee-signature fields and explicitly does not require cosmetic imitation.

issues.finding: The rubric weakened every discrepancy to every material discrepancy.
issues.rationale: The reinforcement row now requires every difference to remain visible and every non-zero difference beyond the stated rounding tolerance to be identified.

issues.finding: Every defensibly comparable item had no auditable comparison population.
issues.rationale: The workbook must now state and apply a scope-and-unit comparability rule to every local estimate item and document plausible excluded matches with reasons.

issues.finding: Ordinary rounding supplied no reproducible reinforcement tolerance.
issues.rationale: The criterion now uses a cited table, displayed unit weight, one rounding step, and a half-unit-in-the-last-displayed-decimal tolerance.

issues.finding: The judge lacks the local and WSDOT source records needed for source-value verification.
issues.rationale: This requires judge-readable source extracts or deterministic checks. Embedding expected quantities, prices, or mappings in the rubric would recreate hidden answers.

issues.finding: The judge lacks portfolio, market, tax, and RMD source records.
issues.rationale: The evaluator must receive compact source data and deterministic calculation checks; the rubric must not encode expected trades or scenario totals.

issues.finding: The judge lacks the original calls, roster, stations, CAD state, and historical source data.
issues.rationale: Source extracts and database-diff checks belong in evaluator infrastructure; embedding expected units, conflicts, or counts would be an answer key.

issues.finding: The judge lacks requisition, bid, benchmark, template, and supplier-term source records.
issues.rationale: The evaluator needs source extracts and deterministic arithmetic checks; hidden supplier totals, award choices, or benchmark matches were not added.

issues.finding: Visual conformance to the provided PO template is not visible in extracted spreadsheet text.
issues.rationale: The rubric now defines observable header, party, logistics, and line-item sections and permits cosmetic variation.

issues.finding: The judge lacks raw and reference data needed to verify exhaustive validation and statistics.
issues.rationale: Compact source tables and deterministic validation and statistical checks must be supplied by the evaluator; expected errors and test results were not embedded.

issues.finding: Standard Jupyter rich outputs are omitted by notebook text extraction.
issues.rationale: The notebook extractor must support text/plain, HTML, streams, errors, and images. Requiring duplicated output prose in the rubric would add an unsupported format burden.

issues.finding: The judge lacks checklist, historical, schedule, room, instructor, and template source records.
issues.rationale: Source extracts and deterministic schedule, ROI, and risk checks are evaluator responsibilities; no expected program, instructor, room, or cost answers were added.

issues.finding: PDF form values and visual checklist annotations may be invisible to text extraction.
issues.rationale: The evaluator must extract form fields and annotations or render pages. The rubric cannot require a text-only reimplementation of an allowed completed PDF.

issues.finding: Use of the Smartsheet workbook as a formatting reference cannot be inferred from extracted values.
issues.rationale: The criterion now evaluates concrete functional fields taken from the attendance template and disclaims cosmetic style matching.
